Give the agent less to guess at: Every account moved onto VOS is one more sending structured, approved orders instead of a voicemail to transcribe. Whatever is parsing the rest has a smaller and messier pile left to work through.

@graph.name: Is VOS a genuine Burnt AI alternative, and is it better than Burnt AI?

acceptedAnswer.text: On order intake the two overlap properly, and on that one job we would say yes: with VOS the buyer approves the order, so correctness is settled by whoever knows the kitchen rather than by a confidence score. Past intake they diverge. Burnt automates purchasing and collections as well, reads channels we never touch, and VOS does none of it. If your shortlist is about getting orders in cleanly, compare them. If it is about automating the office behind that, we are not on the list.

@graph.name: How soon could our accounts be ordering?

acceptedAnswer.text: Most distributors are up and running within 24 to 48 hours, and most kitchens place one the same day. Burnt publishes 1 to 2 weeks for most customers, stretching to 30 to 60 days on complex or legacy systems, which is quick for the amount it is wiring in. Ours is shorter because there is far less to wire, which is the usual reason a Burnt AI alternative gets a look.

@graph.name: Can VOS read orders out of email or WhatsApp?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Burnt does that and lists email, phone, voicemail, WhatsApp, SMS, EDI, portals and spreadsheets. VOS takes the opposite route: instead of decoding whatever arrived, it gives the kitchen an app that turns speech into a list they confirm. If you need those channels parsed, that is a point for them, and better said here than at a demo.

@graph.name: Will VOS take over our ERP?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. It works at the intake end and passes each order on, itemized and approved. Everything after that, picking, invoicing, delivery, runs exactly as it does now in the software you pay for today.

@graph.name: How does VOS price against Burnt?

acceptedAnswer.text: Neither of us publishes a rate card, so this comes down to two quotes. We quote per distributor, once we know what you are running. Burnt quotes after a demo. Worth asking both what the figure covers, because the scope either side of it is very different.

@graph.name: Will anyone need to come to our site?

acceptedAnswer.text: Not for VOS. We set up from the guides you send over, with no implementation project. Burnt describes white-glove onboarding with their team working on your premises, which suits some operations very well and is exactly what others are trying to avoid.

@graph.name: What happens to accounts that will only ever telephone?

acceptedAnswer.text: They keep telephoning and your team handles those as it does today. Be clear about the limit though: a call or a voicemail gets no order number from VOS, no timestamp and no stock movement. Only what comes through the app does.

@graph.name: Where do the Burnt details on this page come from?

acceptedAnswer.text: Burnt's own website, read on 10 October 2026: the agent list and the on-site onboarding line off their homepage, and the channel list, the confidence-threshold wording and the rollout range off their sales and operations product page. We have left their accuracy and time-saving figures out, because those are their numbers to stand behind. If any of it has changed, this page is what needs correcting.
